To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structure of the substrate analogue bound to MurQ-HI shows the location of the key active site residues Glu89, Lys239, and Glu120 and provides a basis for proposing the mechanism of action of MurQ.

we determined the three-dimensional structures of the MurQ-HI and MurQ-EC enzymes, that we identified a potential catalytic base in the active site, and that we identified a mechanism of action for the enzyme.

the MurNAc-6-phosphate hydolase from Haemphilus influenzae has a novel mechanism of action in that the active site acid/base residue is located in the proximity to both the C2 position of the substrate and to the lactyl group at C3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the catalytic mechanism of MurQ and the identification of potential drug targets in bacteria that are resistant to current antimicrobial drugs.
the structure and mechanism of MurQ enzymes.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of MurNAc6P hydrolease and with the development of inhibitors that can be used to block this enzyme in the peptidoylglycan recycling pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism is a concerted general base/general acid mechanism.
the enzyme is a one-base catalyst, and the active site Glu89 is the only active site residue that is involved in both the deprotonation of the substrate and the activation of the water.

the MurQ-HI enzyme is a one-base enzyme in which Glu-89 functions to catalyze both the C-O bond cleavage of the lactyl group and the C-O bond formation of the water molecule, and that this enzyme is a member of a new class of one-base enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MurNAc hydrolases are the first enzymes to be characterized as using an active site glutamic acid to deprotonated the substrate at the C2 and C3 positions, which are the most distant from the carboxylate side chain of the active site residue.
the MurQ-EC enzyme is a member of the MurQ family of MurNAc hydrolases that function via a one-base mechanism.
the crystal structure of MurQ with substrate analogue provides insight into the catalytic mechanism and that this enzyme may be a good candidate for inhibitor development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MurQ enzyme is an unusual enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of a nonlabile ether linkage in the absence of a metal ion or a coenzyme.
the MurQ-HI active site is poised for catalysis, but the mechanism of action remains to be elucidated.
MurQ is a unique enzyme that uses a nonacidic residue to perform an otherwise acid/base catalyzed reaction.
